To: Cedarbrook Pharmacy page
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Important recall: Corvane children’s ibuprofen dosing syringe

If you have Corvane children’s ibuprofen at home, please check the lot number on the bottom of the box.

Corvane Pharma has voluntarily recalled the syringe supplied with two lots of its Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension:

• Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL, berry flavour, 120 mL bottle
• Lot numbers CV6114A and CV6114B
• Expiry 08/2027

The problem is with the printing on the syringe, not the medicine. Corvane says the suspension itself meets specifications and is not contaminated.

On the affected syringes, the volume markings are labelled at half the actual amount. For example, the mark labelled 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL, and the mark labelled 5 mL actually measures 10 mL. Following those markings could mean giving approximately twice the intended dose.

If you have one of these lots:

1. Stop using and discard the syringe that came in the box. Do not try to adjust the dose using that syringe.
2. Use a correctly marked oral syringe to measure any future dose, following the product directions or your health professional’s advice. If you have any doubt about a dose already given, follow the advice below before giving another dose.
3. You can return the product for a full refund. Replacement oral syringes are expected at Cedarbrook today, Monday, before noon. They will be free to anyone who needs one; no receipt is required. We will also be open Saturday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. for exchanges.

If you think your child may have received too much, or you have any doubt about the dose given, please call a poison centre right away. Do not give another dose until the poison centre or your child’s doctor says it is OK. The right advice depends on the child and what they received, so we cannot assess an individual child safely in Facebook comments.

Call 911 or go to the emergency department if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not peeing, or has a seizure.

I know this is frightening, especially if you have already used the syringe. We received the recall notice on the evening of November 6 and put a sign on the door the following morning. Many over-the-counter purchases do not have a patient profile or phone number attached, so we cannot identify and call every customer who bought it. Please share this notice with anyone who may have an affected bottle.
